sections.normalized_html: EXPLANATION
sections.readable_text: EXPLANATION

sections.normalized_html:
The vector [MATH: \mathbf{v}] belongs to [MATH: \textrm{Im}(\mathbf{T})] if there exists a vector [MATH: [x; y; z]] such that [MATH: \mathbf{T}(\mathbf{u}) = \mathbf{v}.]

Therefore, we must have

[MATH: [x + y; − x + y; 2y]|= [4; k; 8].]

This gives the following system of equations: [MATH: {x + y = 4; − x + y = k; 2y = 8.]

From the third equation, we get [MATH: y=4,] which we substitute into the first equation to get [MATH: x + y|= 4; x + 4|= 4; x|= 0.]

Finally, we substitute [MATH: x=0] and [MATH: y=4] into the third equation and obtain [MATH: − x + y|= k; 0 + 4|= k; k|= 4.]

Therefore, [MATH: \mathbf{v}\in\textrm{Im}(\mathbf{T})] when [MATH: k=4.]

[MATH: [2|4|2; 6|4|− 10; 0|4|8]]
sections.readable_text:
The standard matrix [MATH: T] of a linear transformation [MATH: \mathbf{T}] and the vector [MATH: \mathbf{b} \in \mathbb{R}^3] are given below. Determine if there exists a vector [MATH: \mathbf{x} \in \mathbb{R}^3] such that [MATH: \mathbf{T}(\mathbf{x})=\mathbf{b}.] In the affirmative case, find such a vector.

[MATH: [2|4|2; 6|4|− 10; 0|4|8]]

sections.normalized_html: EXPLANATION
sections.readable_text: EXPLANATION

sections.normalized_html:
Since [MATH: T] is the standard matix of [MATH: \mathbf{T},] we have [MATH: \textrm{Im}(\mathbf{T}) = \textrm{Col}(T).] In order to determine whether [MATH: \mathbf{b}] lies in [MATH: \textrm{Im}(\mathbf{T}),] we need to check if the equation [MATH: T\mathbf{x}=\mathbf{b}] is consistent.

So, we find the row echelon form of the augmented matrix [MATH: [T \,|\, \mathbf{b}],] as follows: [MATH: [T|b]|= [2|4|2|6; 6|4|− 10|26; 0|4|8|− 4]|R_{2}:=R_{2} + (− 3)R_{1}; ∼[2|4|2|6; 0|− 8|− 16|8; 0|4|8|− 4]|R_{3}:=R_{3} + (1)/(2)R_{2}; ∼[2|4|2|6; 0|− 8|− 16|8; 0|0|0|0]]

The reduced matrix above has a zero row, and so the system is consistent. We have two pivot columns (the [MATH: 1]st and the [MATH: 2]nd). So, [MATH: x_3] is a free variable. Now, from the second equation, we get

[MATH: -8x_2-16x_3 = 8 \qquad\Longrightarrow\qquad x_2=-1-2x_3.]

Substituting this into the first equation gives

[MATH: 2x_1+4(-1-2x_3)+2x_3 = 6 \qquad\Longrightarrow\qquad x_1=5+3x_3.]

As a result, the general solution is given by [MATH: [5 + 3x_{3}; − 1 − 2x_{3}; x_{3}]]

Setting [MATH: x_3=0,] we have [MATH: [5; − 1; 0]]

Item 2 — Example: Determining a Component of a Vector in the Image of a Linear Transformation

Content:
EXPLANATION

Explanation:
The vector [MATH: \mathbf{v}] belongs to [MATH: \textrm{Im}(\mathbf{T})] if there exists a vector [MATH: [x; y; z]] such that [MATH: \mathbf{T}(\mathbf{u}) = \mathbf{v}.]

Therefore, we must have

[MATH: [x + y; − x + y; 2y]|= [4; k; 8].]

This gives the following system of equations:
[MATH: {x + y = 4; − x + y = k; 2y = 8.]

From the third equation, we get [MATH: y=4,] which we substitute into the first equation to get
[MATH: x + y|= 4; x + 4|= 4; x|= 0.]

Finally, we substitute [MATH: x=0] and [MATH: y=4] into the third equation and obtain
[MATH: − x + y|= k; 0 + 4|= k; k|= 4.]

Therefore, [MATH: \mathbf{v}\in\textrm{Im}(\mathbf{T})] when [MATH: k=4.]

EXPLANATION

So, we find the row echelon form of the augmented matrix [MATH: [T \,|\, \mathbf{b}],] as follows:
[MATH: [T|b]|= [2|4|2|6; 6|4|− 10|26; 0|4|8|− 4]|R_{2}:=R_{2} + (− 3)R_{1}; ∼[2|4|2|6; 0|− 8|− 16|8; 0|4|8|− 4]|R_{3}:=R_{3} + (1)/(2)R_{2}; ∼[2|4|2|6; 0|− 8|− 16|8; 0|0|0|0]]

Now, from the second equation, we get

[MATH: -8x_2-16x_3 = 8
\qquad\Longrightarrow\qquad
x_2=-1-2x_3.]

Substituting this into the first equation gives

[MATH: 2x_1+4(-1-2x_3)+2x_3 = 6
\qquad\Longrightarrow\qquad
x_1=5+3x_3.]

As a result, the general solution is given by
[MATH: [5 + 3x_{3}; − 1 − 2x_{3}; x_{3}]]

Setting [MATH: x_3=0,] we have
[MATH: [5; − 1; 0]]
